name: copado-release-assistant
description: Copado release work for Salesforce metadata and code: resolve promotion conflicts - metadata element by element, Apex and Lightning web components by member - validate exactly what each stage deploys from the branch, follow a story through the pipeline, follow Copado deployments - plus package.xml from commit JSON, three-way merges and deploy-breaking checks.

commands.title: Show Section Order for This Type
Generate package.xml from Copado Commit JSON
Validate User Story from Its Feature Branch

cmr.project.path.markdownDescription: The Salesforce project to work in - the folder holding `sfdx-project.json`. **Leave empty to find it automatically**: the project of the file you have open, the open folder, or the single project inside it. Set it when the open folder holds several projects. Absolute, or relative to the open folder.

cmr.package.outputFolder.description: Where package.xml, package-retrieve.xml and destructiveChanges.xml are written, relative to the workspace.
cmr.package.outputFolder.markdownDescription: Folder in the project for the generated `package.xml` (and `destructiveChanges.xml` when there are deletions). Relative to the project root; an existing `package.xml` there is replaced. Paths outside the project are not allowed.

cmr.storage.folder.markdownDescription: The extension's own working folder, inside the project: merge views, branch versions and the retrieve-only manifest. It contains a `.gitignore` of `*`, so nothing in it is ever committed and your project's `.gitignore` is left alone. Never use a package directory such as `force-app`.

cmr.storage.keepDays.markdownDescription: Working files the extension fetched - branch comparisons, promotion files, manual merges, reports - are removed by themselves once nothing in them has changed for this many days. Never the open merge’s, nor a promotion’s with resolutions not uploaded to Copado yet. `0`: never; **Clean Working Files** empties it all at once.

cmr.merge.applyFormatting.markdownDescription: Order and sort the merged file using the **Formatting** settings. Turn off to keep the target's own order: new entries are appended, nothing is reordered. Only affects merges - `Format Document` is unchanged.

enumDescriptions: The incoming file's value is used, and you can switch to the target's.
The target's value is used, and you can switch to the incoming one.
cmr.merge.conflictWinner.description: Which value a real conflict starts with, before you review it.

enumDescriptions: The merged result for permission sets, profiles, labels and translations - files often retrieved in part, where an entry the feature branch lacks is not a removal; the feature branch's file for everything else (objects, pages, layouts, flows, code...), so its removals count.
The feature branch's file as it is.
The target branch's file as it is.
Both branches combined: nothing of the target is dropped.
cmr.merge.startFrom.markdownDescription: Where your resolution starts when you open a merge. Whatever the start, the merge editor marks what the other branch has - including what the feature branch does not have - and you switch with **Start from** in the merge editor.

cmr.merge.hideIdentical.markdownDescription: In the merge editor, fold away runs of lines that are the same on both sides, keeping 3 lines around each change. **Hide identical** in its toolbar switches it, and the choice is kept here.

cmr.merge.removeDuplicates.description: Remove duplicate entries while merging. Duplicates are the only thing a merge ever removes, and every removal is listed in the output panel.

cmr.merge.normalizeBeforeDiff.description: Order and reindent both files before showing the diff, so the comparison shows real differences instead of reordering noise. Strongly recommended for retrieved profiles and permission sets.

cmr.merge.alwaysKeepTarget.markdownDescription: Parts of the file that must always come from the target, never from the incoming file. Use a tag name (`userLicense`), a path (`fields/description`) or a type-qualified path (`Profile/loginIpRanges`). A collection listed here keeps the target's entries and ignores the incoming ones entirely. Useful for environment-specific sections: `["loginIpRanges", "loginHours", "tabVisibilities"]`.

cmr.dedupe.keep.description: Which occurrence survives when duplicates are removed.

cmr.merge.useAncestor.markdownDescription: For **metadata**: use the common ancestor when it is known - Copado’s own, or the merge-base of the feature branch and the destination branch from the connected repository - so the merge editor marks what each branch did since. Code needs none: Copado’s conflict file is git’s merge, made with it.

enumDescriptions: The merge editor: Copado’s conflict file as git merged it - each conflict shown both ways, Accept target, Accept feature or Accept both; the markers never shown.
VS Code’s own conflict view, with Accept Current, Incoming or Both.
cmr.merge.codeIn.markdownDescription: Where a promotion’s **code** conflicts open - Apex, JavaScript, a component’s template, CSS, Visualforce and Aura.

enumDescriptions: One panel: your resolution - Copado’s conflict file, its conflicts marked.
Two panel: the target beside your resolution, the same conflicts over it.
cmr.merge.codeView.markdownDescription: How the merge editor shows **code**. Switch it in the editor’s **View** menu – that changes this setting. Metadata is always shown in two panels.

cmr.format.elementOrder.description: standard writes elements in the order Salesforce uses - fullName first, then alphabetical - so a retrieved file is left unchanged. alphabetical is the same without fullName first; preserve keeps the file's own order. Use cmr.format.typeOrder to put chosen elements first.

cmr.format.sortCollections.description: Sort entries inside collections where order carries no meaning, such as fieldPermissions. Order-sensitive collections like layout sections and picklist values are never sorted.

cmr.format.typeOrder.markdownDescription: Top-level section order per metadata type, for example `{ "PermissionSet": ["label", "description", "objectPermissions"] }`. The tags you list come first, in exactly that order; everything you leave out follows alphabetically. Overrides the built-in order for that type. Run **Copado Merge: Show Section Order for This Type** to get a snippet to edit.

cmr.format.leadingElements.markdownDescription: Extra tags to pull to the very top of a file, per metadata type, in the order listed - applied on top of whichever order won. Use `*` for every type. Most of the time `#cmr.format.typeOrder#` is the setting you want; this one is for a quick hoist without restating an order.

cmr.format.indent.description: Spaces per level. The Metadata API uses 4.

cmr.format.removeDuplicatesOnFormat.description: Also drop duplicate entries when formatting.

cmr.diagnostics.enable.description: Report duplicate metadata entries as you type.

cmr.diagnostics.duplicateSeverity.description: Severity for duplicates. Entries that share a key but differ in value are always errors, because the deployment will fail.

cmr.diagnostics.warnRepeatedSingletons.description: Report scalar elements that appear more than once, such as two <description> tags after a bad merge.

cmr.rules.enable.description: Check for structural problems that would fail a deployment but are not duplicates: a field that is editable but not readable, two default record types on one object, the same field twice on a layout, and similar.

cmr.rules.disabled.markdownDescription: Rule ids to switch off, e.g. `["permissions.fieldWithoutObject"]`. The id of each finding is shown in the Problems panel and in the merge panel.

cmr.diagnostics.largeFileKb.description: Files bigger than this (in KB) are only re-checked once typing settles, instead of after every keystroke. Set to 0 to always check immediately.

cmr.package.apiVersion.markdownDescription: API version for generated manifests. Empty uses `sourceApiVersion` from `sfdx-project.json`, then 62.0.

cmr.package.actionMapping.markdownDescription: How each Copado action becomes part of the package. `deploy` - in package.xml. `selective` - in package.xml, for Copado **selective commits**: validations from a branch deploy the committed version; from the project, its version is deployed as it is. `retrieve` - left out of package.xml (Copado only retrieves these). `destructive` - deleted. `ignore` - left out.

cmr.package.warnStandardFields.description: Warn when standard fields (no __c suffix) are about to be deployed. Most cannot be.

cmr.copado.org.markdownDescription: Alias or username of the **Copado org** - the Salesforce org where Copado runs - logged in with the Salesforce CLI (`sf org login web --alias copado`). Everything the extension reads from Copado - promotions, stories, the pipeline, releases, deployments - comes from here.

cmr.copado.environmentOrgs.markdownDescription: Which Salesforce CLI login stands for each Copado environment, by environment name - for example `{ "QA": "qa" }`. Validations for a stage run as this login, and the page shows it. Filled in the first time an environment cannot be matched by its org credential’s username.

cmr.promotion.keepDays.markdownDescription: Days to keep a finished promotion's local files - every conflict uploaded or resolved in Copado - after it was last refreshed. `0` keeps them until you close the promotion.

cmr.copado.watchSeconds.markdownDescription: While Copado deploys a promotion, how often (in seconds) the Deployment tab reads its job records again. Read-only; it stops when the job finishes or the page closes.

cmr.copado.recreateBranchField.markdownDescription: The API name of Copado’s **Re-create promotion branch** checkbox on the promotion. Empty finds it by itself - a checkbox whose name or label says re-create (or rebuild) and branch. Set it only if your Copado version calls it something else.

cmr.promotion.autoResolve.markdownDescription: Resolve automatically the conflict files that need no decision - the sides agree, or only one side changed - so they are ready to upload without you. **Off** (the default): nothing is resolved without you; a clean merge is offered as a suggestion that you review and accept, and code keeps every conflict block for you to decide.

cmr.repo.url.markdownDescription: The address of the repository Copado commits to. **Leave empty to take it from Copado’s Git Repository record**: the first validation from a branch asks only for the read-only token. Azure DevOps, GitHub, GitLab and Bitbucket Cloud; the token is kept in VS Code’s encrypted secret storage.

cmr.repo.provider.markdownDescription: Which host the address belongs to. `auto` recognises dev.azure.com, *.visualstudio.com, github.com, gitlab.com and bitbucket.org; pick it for a self-hosted Azure DevOps Server, GitHub Enterprise or GitLab.

cmr.repo.featureBranch.markdownDescription: The branch a user story’s commits are on, with `{story}` for its number - Copado’s convention is `feature/{story}`. When a Copado record of the story names its branch, that name is used instead.

cmr.repo.promotionBranch.markdownDescription: The branch Copado builds for a promotion, with `{promotion}` for its name (for example `P12345`). **Validate promotion branch** reads the promotion’s components from it.

cmr.git.targetBranch.description: The branch that keeps everything - usually the environment branch you promote into, for example qa or uat. Empty asks each time.

cmr.git.incomingBranch.description: The branch being promoted, for example dev or a feature branch. Its values win a real conflict. Empty asks each time and suggests the branch you are on.

cmr.git.remote.description: Remote used when a branch is not present locally, and for fetching.

cmr.git.fetchFirst.description: Fetch from the remote before comparing, so remote branches are current.

cmr.git.confirmBranches.description: Show the branch pickers each time, with the settings above pre-selected. Turn off to go straight to the comparison.

cmr.git.includeBothChanged.description: Also list files both branches changed that git can merge on its own. A line-by-line merge of metadata XML can still produce duplicates.

cmr.git.metadataOnly.description: Hide files that are not Salesforce metadata XML.

cmr.sf.path.description: The Salesforce CLI executable. Orgs come from what you have authorised with it - no credentials are stored by this extension.

cmr.org.target.description: Alias or username of the org to validate against. Empty asks each time.

cmr.org.confirm.description: Show the org pickers each time, with the settings above pre-selected.

enumDescriptions: When the package contains Apex, ask which test classes to run, pre-selecting the ones in the package.
Run the test classes in the package plus Default Tests, without asking.
cmr.validate.testLevel.description: Test level when the package contains Apex.

cmr.validate.testLevelWithoutApex.description: Test level when the package has no Apex. NoTestRun runs a check-only 'sf project deploy start --dry-run', because 'deploy validate' does not accept NoTestRun. RunLocalTests uses 'deploy validate' and runs every local test.
enumDescriptions: Check-only deployment, no tests. Fast - right for sandboxes.
Check-only deployment running all local tests. Slow.

cmr.validate.testClassPattern.description: Regular expression that marks an Apex class in the package as a test class, to pre-select it.

cmr.validate.defaultTests.description: Test classes always offered when the package contains Apex.

cmr.validate.waitMinutes.description: How long to wait for a retrieve or validation before giving up.

cmr.validate.warnOnProduction.description: Confirm before validating against an org that does not look like a sandbox.

cmr.validate.revealOutput.description: Open the output panel when a retrieve or validation starts, so the Salesforce CLI's own progress - stages, component and test counts - is visible as it happens.

cmr.validate.progressInterval.markdownDescription: `0` (default): when the CLI reprints its progress block, the output panel shows the **whole block only when its text or values change** - a stage finishing, Pending becoming Succeeded, `Components: 12/27` moving. Spinner glyphs (`| / - \`) and ticking timers are not changes; they show live in the progress notification. Set a number of seconds to also show an unchanged block that often.

cmr.validate.skipSourceTracking.markdownDescription: Skip the CLI's source-tracking step (it sets `SF_DISABLE_SOURCE_MEMBER_POLLING=true` for retrieves and validations). After a retrieve completes, the CLI normally polls the org's SourceMember object to update its local tracking; this extension overwrites files by design, so that step only adds time. If you also use tracked commands such as a plain `sf project retrieve start` in this project, run `sf project reset tracking` afterwards, or turn this off.

cmr.output.maskIdentities.markdownDescription: Mask usernames, email addresses, org and user ids and My Domain addresses in the output panel and in copied reports - useful before pasting logs into a ticket. Session tokens are always masked.

cmr.guard.allowedTargetOrgs.markdownDescription: Orgs that may be validated against, by alias or username; `*` is a wildcard, and `production` / `sandbox` match by org kind. Empty allows any org. A `copado-policy.json` file at the project root, when present, replaces all guardrail settings.

cmr.guard.blockedTargetOrgs.markdownDescription: Orgs that may never be validated against. Wins over the allowed list.

cmr.guard.allowProduction.markdownDescription: Allow validating against production orgs at all. Validation is always check-only.

cmr.guard.minimumTestLevel.markdownDescription: Lowest test level per org pattern, for example `{ "production": "RunLocalTests" }`. A lower choice is raised automatically, and the output says so.

cmr.guard.environments.markdownDescription: Rules per Copado environment, by its name - for example `{ "UAT": { "minimumTestLevel": "RunLocalTests", "coverage": 85 }, "Production": { "requiredTargetUser": "release.user@*" } }`. `requiredTargetUser` is the login a validation for that stage must use (`*` is a wildcard); `coverage` the lowest per-class coverage for the Apex in the package. A `copado-policy.json` with an `environments` block replaces this.

cmr.http.proxy.markdownDescription: Proxy for the Copado org and the Git host, such as `http://proxy.example.com:8080` or `http://user:password@proxy:8080`. Empty uses VS Code’s **Http: Proxy**, then `HTTPS_PROXY`. `NO_PROXY` is honoured; this machine (`localhost`) is never proxied.

cmr.http.caFile.markdownDescription: A PEM file of extra certificates to trust, for a proxy that inspects TLS with its own certificate. VS Code’s **Http: Proxy Strict SSL** also applies through a proxy.

viewsWelcome.contents:
Resolve a Copado promotion, follow a story through the pipeline and check deployments - all on one page.
[Open Release Assistant](command:cmr.page.open)
Also: [validate a deployment](command:cmr.validate.run), [build a package.xml from a commit](command:cmr.package.fromCommit), [check branch conflicts](command:cmr.git.check).

untrustedWorkspaces.description: In a folder you have not trusted, the extension does not run the Salesforce CLI or git: retrieve, validation, branch conflicts and Copado downloads are turned off. Merging, formatting and checks still work.
